open_items.text: Review a sanitised StandaloneSlot fixture before it is committed - the filename embeds the operator roleId, so it needs a rename not just redaction
Capture safety depends on a privacy toggle in the game menu and nothing here can detect its state - decide whether that is documentable or guardable

ENCODING: some TS.UI log lines carry CJK text, so a log excerpt is not ASCII and not single-byte. Confirm the redactor and every excerpt path handle it, and that the ASCII hygiene guard can never be fed raw log text

Dungeon log lines carry the operator persona under a player-name key AND the roleid in the SAME line as loot values, so any dungeon excerpt is dense with PII. Verify the redactor covers both key shapes before item 1 commits a fixture

GAP MEASURED 2026-08-09: the pre-commit hook ACCEPTED a commit that tests/test_no_pii.py then rejected - the hook is less strict than the test, so a hazard can land and only fail later in the suite. Decide whether the hook should run the same detectors

MEASURED: .githooks/pre-commit ASCII arm does not cover *.json - a json em-dash gives HOOK EXIT 0 while the same bytes in a .md are BLOCKED. lanes/*.STATE.json are the repo first tracked agent-written json, so this gap is now load-bearing

RE-SCOPED FROM SAF-3 and remeasured 2026-08-11: prefix sharing is NOT the worst of it. The operator roleId (19 digits) appears VERBATIM 5 times in the StandaloneSlot save (2 slot names, 3 ownerRoleId in ItemCell JSON), 5 further distinct ids share 17 of its 19 digits, and BattleId shares 12 - not the 14 recorded earlier, which is refuted across all 250 captured generations. A 2b fixture must renumber EVERY 19-digit id, not just mask the roleId

PvP BLIND SPOT: LeaderRankScoreData carries KillPlayerHistoryDatas plus KillPlayerCount and teamKillPlayerCount. It holds no player identifier in the captured run because that run was solo, so a clean scan of it is evidence about solo play only. A fixture taken from a run with real players must be rescanned for third-party names and ids, never assumed clean on this precedent

CORRECTED 2026-08-11: Unreal Blueprint property names Name_Index_<32 hex GUID> trip PRODUCTUSERID 772 times and LONG_ID 62 of 100 times. Last slice said the fixture should AUTHOR its GUIDs - that is not sufficient as written. The hex rule keys on SHAPE and cannot tell an authored GUID from a real puid, so an authored GUID that is still 32 hex characters changes nothing. It must stop being a hex run. Verified on the real save: replacing every 32-hex run with a non-hex string takes PRODUCTUSERID to 0 and LONG_ID from 100 to 38. Neither rule is narrowed

MEASURED THIRD-PARTY PII, promoted from the SAF-10 risk: LeaderRankScoreData.KillPlayerHistoryDatas holds one record of ten fields, three of them unbounded strings - PlayerName, MsgSubChannelString, MsgAppearanceString. In this capture IsBot is true so the name is a generated bot, which is luck not a guarantee; in a run with real players PlayerName holds a third party's display name. NO CONTENT RULE CAN REACH IT - GVAS has no key/value separator, so keyed rules and persona discovery are structurally blind, and a display name has no shape for a shape rule to match. Covered instead by the structural NAME_FIELD rule: these three properties must carry AUTHORED_NAME_MARKER in any committed artifact. Fires 3 times on the real save; goes quiet when the values are authored

WIRING GAP, stated rather than assumed: NAME_FIELD reaches the tree scan only because tests/test_no_pii.py calls iter_sensitive, which now walks DETECT_ONLY_RULES. Nothing asserts that a FIXTURE specifically was checked - the scan covers whatever is committed. When the 2b fixture lands, add a test that names the fixture file and asserts NAME_FIELD is silent on it, so the check cannot be lost by moving or renaming the file

open_items.blocked_on: a capture containing a NameProperty or TextProperty
open_items.text: UNMEASURED BY CONSTRUCTION: NAME_BEARING_TYPES now covers NameProperty and TextProperty as well as StrProperty, added by reasoning about the GVAS format rather than by measurement - neither token appears in any captured save. Two things need re-measuring if one is ever observed. (1) A TextProperty's value sits behind an FText header (flags, history type, namespace and key FStrings) rather than directly after the 8-byte size and the has-guid byte, so the authored marker may fall outside the 48-byte window and the rule would then be unsatisfiable for that token. (2) The same window is what stops an authored neighbour authorising an unauthored field, so it cannot simply be widened without re-checking field spacing.

resume_note: NAME_FIELD re-armed after a P0 self-inflicted defect - redact() had disarmed it. Next is still the 2b fixture against SAF-8, SAF-9, SAF-11 and SAF-12, plus SAF-13 on the unmeasured type tokens
